Suraya: Burnt Alive

By: Anina Peens | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The mysterious deaths of Suraya Deedat and her four children may finally be solved as private prosecutor Gerrie Nel, takes on this decade old case

Unique Selling Point:
No one has ever been able to tell the true story of what transpired on the night Suraya Deedat and her four children died and their family home in Johannesburg was torched to ashes along with their remains. But now, nine years after their deaths, some questions may finally be answered.

Summary:
The family of Suraya Deedat may finally get some answers in November after nearly a decade of questions. The inquest into the deaths of Suraya and her four small children will wrap up in the Johannesburg magistrates court. The inquest was opened by private prosecutor Gerrie Nel at the beginning of 2020. Five witnesses have been called to the stand by Nel and the defense team. The last witness who will testify in November is the pathologist who performed the autopsies. She will testify whether there were traces of smoke in the lungs of the family members. This information will assist in ascertaining whether the family was killed before the fire scorched their house or if they did indeed burn to death.

Further information:
It has been 9 years and the family of Suraya Deedat is still looking for answers. The bodies of the 37-year-old mother and all four of her small children were found in their burnt-out home in Johannesburg. They were lying in a row in the lounge of the family home in Ormonde. All of them were lying on their backs facing the ceiling indicating that they were not close to an exit or escape at the time of the fire.
The husband and father, Naeem Deedat escaped the house unharmed through a bathroom window. His clothes were not burnt and the bathroom from which he escaped was locked off from the rest of the house. A fridge was also found blocking the lounge door where the family was found.
Naeem stated in an affidavit (that he changed 3 times) that the fire was started by a pillow that fell onto an electric heater. Naeem maintains to date that he could not save his family as the pillow ignited a fire that rapidly turned into a massive inferno.

In 2017, Suraya’s family approached private investigator Paul O’Sullivan who opened the first inquest. But O’Sullivan was unable to decipher what happened on the night of the family’s deaths. The court ruled out murder and O’Sullivan dropped the case. His investigations however led him to Jacob Polela, a witness who later became central to the second inquest that was opened by private prosecutor, Gerrie Nel three years later.

In February 2020 the second inquest started in the Johannesburg Magistrates court.
Nel called various witnesses to the stand, including Jacob Polela. Polela alleges that he saw Naeem outside the house on the night of the fire. He testified that Naeem was looking into the house which was heavily locked from the outside.

The inquest was halted before the lockdown as the court waited on the pathologist who performed the autopsies, to testify. The pathologist resides in Canada and will be testifying via Zoom in November.

Press Release:


Waiting to Exhale: Inquest into the death of Suraya Deedat
In 2011, Suraya Deedat and her four young children were found dead after a fire tore through their Johannesburg home. There was no signs of any attempt made by the mother to escape the burning house and save her children while the husband and father managed to escape unharmed. Investigations into the incident concluded that the fire was an accident caused by an electric heater. Now, nearly ten years later, Suraya’s family is back in court, hoping that a renewed inquest will finally bring them the closure they need.
Producer: Anina Peens | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

Script:


Suraya: Burnt Alive Draft Script 5

VO
Some people call it the devils blaze…

UPSOUND
DRONE 0123 FLIES OVER MOSQUE AND SETTLES OVER HOUSE

VO
When they talk about the night a raging fire swallowed an entire family alive. The youngest being only six months old.

VO
But everything about this fire and the way in which the family reacted to it, was strange.

UPSOUND
FADE OUT DRONE AND FADE IN CAMERA SHOT OF HOUSE
CLAIRE LOOKS AT HOUSE AND THEN INTO CAMERA

LINK:
“In a house in the South of Johannesburg, a mother and her four young children were found dead, lying on their backs in a row after a fire tore through their house. Nine years later and her family is still looking for answers”

SUPER@ NASEEMA AHMED, MOTHER OF DECEASED
“It was terrible. I’ll never forget that day, never”

VO
Naseema Ahmed’s relentless search to find answers surrounding the deaths of her daughter, Suraya Deedat and her four grandchildren, finally led to a renewed inquest in 2020. Police investigations and a previous inquest into the case concluded that the fire was an accident caused by a pillow that fell onto an electric heater in the children’s bedroom.

Link
An inquest is not a criminal or civil case. It is evidence led in court that helps the state to decide whether there are grounds for prosecution.

VO
The inquest was opened because Suraya’s family doesnt believe that the fire was an accident.

SUPER@ NASEEMA AHMED, MOTHER OF DECEASED
“Nine years, I am like a living dead person. I think every day what happened, what happened. I know for a fact something went wrong.
SUPER@ NASEEMA AHMED, MOTHER OF DECEASED
Why? Why didn’t Suraya herself take one of her kids and threw them out of the house? Even if they broke an arm and leg that’s fine. But why wasn’t she able to do that?”

Link
The question they also want an answer to, is how it could be possible that only one person was freed from the burning house on the night of the incident.

VO
Husband and father, Naeem Deedat escaped without a scratch.

SUPER@ REHANA ISMAEL, SISTER AND AUNT OF DECEASED
“He was supposed to be there, and his job was to protect his family, come what may. An animal will protect its young, but he didn’t do that. That makes me very angry, I am angry at him because he needs to give us the answers that we are looking for. He is the only one that was there.”

VO
Naeem says there was no way the family was able to escape during the fire.

SUPER@ NAEEM DEEDAT, FATHER AND HUSBAND
“I was woken up by Suraya and she was screaming, we must move we must move….when I got to the room, the room was on fire and I said to Suraya she must take the kids out. That fire developed so quickly…

VO
Naeem says while fighting the fire, it became impossible to breathe and that he had to save himself.

He escaped the house through a bathroom window with the help of a neighbor.

SUPER@MUKTHAR AHMED, FATHER OF DECEASED
“The neighbor phoned me eleven at night, no two in the morning sorry. He said he is Suraya and Naeem’s neighbor and he said I phone to inform you the house got on fire. And then when I got there, I see that the smoke is coming out and there was nothing left, and he was standing outside. So, when I asked Naeem, where is my daughter and my grandchildren and he started stammering. He said I don’t know whether they took them out or whether they’re still inside.”

VO
Naeem says neither him or Suraya were able to phone for help during the incident as their phones were out of reach.

SUPER@ NAEEM DEEDAT, FATHER AND HUSBAND
“When I got out, the owner of the house was there and I took her phone and I phoned Suraya’s parents.”

VO
But Suraya’s family says they battle to understand why there was no evidence of any effort made by Suraya to escape the house or to save her children.

SUPER@ABDUL AHMED, BROTHER AND UNCLE OF DECEASED
“So, I don’t understand, there was metal objects, there was a dumbbell that was lying next to the glass door that she could have picked up and throw through the glass and they would have been free…”

SUPER@ NASEEMA AHMED, MOTHER OF DECEASED
“I don’t think anybody really investigated this case. The police have failed me. My case was jumping from this station to that station from this station to that station…”

VO
Their search for closure finally led Suraya’s family to Adv Gerrie Nel, the former state prosecutor who put Paralympian gold medalist, Oscar Pistorius behind bars for the murder of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp in 2014.

SUPER@ADV GERRIE NEL
“For the system to fail a family like them, a humble family, people that love their children… it is a very close-knit family, mother and her two daughters talking every day and then this happens and there is no closure and there is no closure after nine years…”

VO
Since the night of the fire and same day burial of Suraya and the children, Naeem broke all contact with Suraya’s family.

SUPER@ NASEEMA AHMED, MOTHER OF DECEASED
“Sometimes I’m sitting outside and I’m looking towards Suraya’s road and I used to sometimes see his car going past and he used to bend and looked but he never stopped. He thought nothing about us”

VO
Naeem says the family blames him for the incident because they cannot accept what happened.

SUPER@ NAEEM DEEDAT, FATHER AND HUSBAND
“I don’t think they want closure, if they wanted closure the previous inquest would have given it to them. They want to see my behind bars”

Link
Naeem stated that the pillow falling onto the heater caused such a rapid uncontrollable blaze, that he was unable to save his family.
A scenario described in by a fire expert as highly unlikely.

SUPER@DANIEL JOUBERT, FIRE EXPERT
“This fire, according to all of my experience, and I was an operational fireman 1979 till 2002 and I have seen many fires and I can tell you know, I can say with absolute certainty that this fire was abnormally fast.”

VO
Joubert’s evidence led by Nel during the inquest was based on an analysis made 8 years after the fire.

SUPER@ADV GERRIE NEL
“We have asked him to give us an expert opinion based on his knowledge of fire dynamics. So, what happens in a fire, how people react…now that is indispensable in matters like this to get to a probable course and the effect of a fire”

VO
Joubert says he didn’t have to be on the scene to draw conclusions from the evidence provided. He says the behavior of the family during the fire is unheard of.

SUPER@DANIEL JOUBERT, FIRE EXPERT
“It so unlikely to find a mother and four children totally divorced from each other in a row, in a half moon. A six-month-old baby not in its mothers’ arms, mother is not crouched over it trying to protect it, they are separate from each other. At least four of those people were on their backs at the time of the fire, you don’t do that. the least that that mother would have done is get her children to the nearest window or the furthest window.

VO
In court, Nel raised the question of an accelerant being used in the fire. Something the fire expert says, he suspects.

SUPER@DANIEL JOUBERT, FIRE EXPERT
“There was a five-liter container found in the backyard of this house and the fire officer who responded to that fire found this, opened it and smelled it, and he smelled petrol. He put it back exactly where it was and reported it to the police…”

SUPER@NAEEM DEEDAT, FATHER AND HUSBAND
“That same fire expert cannot produce a photo from all the hundreds of photos they have. Remember, somebody is paying that fire expert.”

VO
An eyewitness who passed by the house on the late afternoon before the incident testified during the inquest, that he allegedly saw the couple have an argument outside the house on the afternoon before the fire. He said that he was picking up recycling materials from the Deedat’s front yard when he heard Naeem shouting at Suraya.

VO
Suraya’s mother says she saw that there was tension between Naeem and Suraya the day before the fire.

SUPER@ NASEEMA AHMED, MOTHER OF DECEASED
“The night before the incident she left the kids by me and I could see the tension between the husband and wife, but I did not ask what the problem is because I said they will sort it out”

VO
Naeem says this is a lie and that him and Suraya had no marital problems.

SUPER@NAEEM DEEDAT, FATHER AND HUSBAND OF DECEASED
“Everything was ok, we were happy go lucky…”

VO
The Pathologist who was called to the scene on the night of the incident told the court that she did not find anything out of the ordinary about the house fire. Dr Candice Hansmeyer testified electronically from Canada where she now resides.

UPSOUND

SUPER@ DR CANDICE HANSMEYER, PATHOLOGIST
“During the autopsies the tissues all had that characteristic pink discoloration which is highly suggestive of carbon monoxide toxicity. Whether they were unconscious or spontaneously breathing we could not tell.”

VO
Nazley January, leading evidence for the state, asked Dr Hansmeyer whether any traces of an accelerant such as petrol was found on the bodies or clothing of the victims. Dr Hansmeyer said she didn’t deem it necessary at the time to call in the services of a toxologist and therefore such a report is not available. January further questioned the position in which the bodies were found.

UPSOUND
SUPER@ NAZLEY JANUARY, STATE EVIDENCE LEADER
“All of these bodies were found approximately one meter apart, would it have been normal for them to have been spread out in this fashion? I would have expected them to all be in one corner, with the mom”

VO
Dr Hansmeyer said she could not insinuate anything from the way in which the bodies were lying. She did however say that she also finds it strange that Naeem escaped unharmed.

SUPER@ DR CANDICE HANSMEYER, PATHOLOGIST
“I do remember that what struck me as being weird was that the father who was in the building did not incur any burns”

SUPER@ NAZLEY JANUARY, STATE EVIDENCE LEADER
“Are you able to comment on his demeanor on that particular day?”

SUPER@ DR CANDICE HANSMEYER, PATHOLOGIST
“Yes, the father seemed quite calm.”

SUPER@NAEEM DEEDAT, FATHER AND HUSBAND
Initially it doesn’t hit you, when you are still on the scene and there are still people on the scene. It only hits you a day or two later when you realize, they are gone now.”

VO
Adv Paul Jorgensohn for the Deedat family stated to Dr Hansmeyer that no two people’s reaction in a situation like this will be the same.

SUPER@ PAUL JORGENSOHN, COUNCIL FOR DEEDAT FAMILY
“You don’t know whether the father was given a tranquilizer? You don’t know?”

SUPER@ DR CANDICE HANSMEYER, PATHOLOGIST
“I have no idea, I have no information, it is purely my opinion (intuition).

LINK
Closing arguments are set to be heard in 2021 from where the state will decide whether the fire was indeed an accident or whether someone is responsible for the deaths of 32 year old Suraya, 6 months old Zubair, 2 year old Laaiqa, four year old Fathima and Uzair who was 5 years old at the time of their deaths.

At least four of those people were on their backs at the time of the fire, you don’t do that. the least that that mother would have done is get her children to the nearest window or the furthest window. VO In court, Nel raised the question of an accelerant being used in the fire. Something the fire expert says, he suspects. SUPER@DANIEL JOUBERT, FIRE EXPERT “There was a five-liter container found in the backyard of this house and the fire officer who responded to that fire found this, opened it and smelled it, and he smelled petrol. He put it back exactly where it was and reported it to the police…” SUPER@NAEEM DEEDAT, FATHER AND HUSBAND “That same fire expert cannot produce a photo from all the hundreds of photos they have. Remember, somebody is paying that fire expert.” VO An eyewitness who passed by the house on the late afternoon before the incident testified during the inquest, that he allegedly saw the couple have an argument outside the house on the afternoon before the fire. He said that he was picking up recycling materials from the Deedat’s front yard when he heard Naeem shouting at Suraya. VO Suraya’s mother says she saw that there was tension between Naeem and Suraya the day before the fire. SUPER@ NASEEMA AHMED, MOTHER OF DECEASED “The night before the incident she left the kids by me and I could see the tension between the husband and wife, but I did not ask what the problem is because I said they will sort it out” VO Naeem says this is a lie and that him and Suraya had no marital problems. SUPER@NAEEM DEEDAT, FATHER AND HUSBAND OF DECEASED “Everything was ok, we were happy go lucky…” VO The Pathologist who was called to the scene on the night of the incident told the court that she did not find anything out of the ordinary about the house fire. Dr Candice Hansmeyer testified electronically from Canada where she now resides. UPSOUND SUPER@ DR CANDICE HANSMEYER, PATHOLOGIST “During the autopsies the tissues all had that characteristic pink discoloration which is highly suggestive of carbon monoxide toxicity. Whether they were unconscious or spontaneously breathing we could not tell.” VO Nazley January, leading evidence for the state, asked Dr Hansmeyer whether any traces of an accelerant such as petrol was found on the bodies or clothing of the victims. Dr Hansmeyer said she didn’t deem it necessary at the time to call in the services of a toxologist and therefore such a report is not available. January further questioned the position in which the bodies were found. UPSOUND SUPER@ NAZLEY JANUARY, STATE EVIDENCE LEADER “All of these bodies were found approximately one meter apart, would it have been normal for them to have been spread out in this fashion? I would have expected them to all be in one corner, with the mom” VO Dr Hansmeyer said she could not insinuate anything from the way in which the bodies were lying. She did however say that she also finds it strange that Naeem escaped unharmed. SUPER@ DR CANDICE HANSMEYER, PATHOLOGIST “I do remember that what struck me as being weird was that the father who was in the building did not incur any burns” SUPER@ NAZLEY JANUARY, STATE EVIDENCE LEADER “Are you able to comment on his demeanor on that particular day?” SUPER@ DR CANDICE HANSMEYER, PATHOLOGIST “Yes, the father seemed quite calm.” SUPER@NAEEM DEEDAT, FATHER AND HUSBAND Initially it doesn’t hit you, when you are still on the scene and there are still people on the scene. It only hits you a day or two later when you realize, they are gone now.” VO Adv Paul Jorgensohn for the Deedat family stated to Dr Hansmeyer that no two people’s reaction in a situation like this will be the same. SUPER@ PAUL JORGENSOHN, COUNCIL FOR DEEDAT FAMILY “You don’t know whether the father was given a tranquilizer? You don’t know?” SUPER@ DR CANDICE HANSMEYER, PATHOLOGIST “I have no idea, I have no information, it is purely my opinion (intuition). LINK Closing arguments are set to be heard in 2021 from where the state will decide whether the fire was indeed an accident or whether someone is responsible for the deaths of 32 year old Suraya, 6 months old Zubair, 2 year old Laaiqa, four year old Fathima and Uzair who was 5 years old at the time of their deaths.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The mysterious deaths of Suraya Deedat and her four children may finally be solved as private prosecutor Gerrie Nel, takes on this decade old case
metadata.Unique Selling Point: No one has ever been able to tell the true story of what transpired on the night Suraya Deedat and her four children died and their family home in Johannesburg was torched to ashes along with their remains. But now, nine years after their deaths, some questions may finally be answered.
metadata.Summary: The family of Suraya Deedat may finally get some answers in November after nearly a decade of questions. The inquest into the deaths of Suraya and her four small children will wrap up in the Johannesburg magistrates court. The inquest was opened by private prosecutor Gerrie Nel at the beginning of 2020. Five witnesses have been called to the stand by Nel and the defense team. The last witness who will testify in November is the pathologist who performed the autopsies. She will testify whether there were traces of smoke in the lungs of the family members. This information will assist in ascertaining whether the family was killed before the fire scorched their house or if they did indeed burn to death.
metadata.Further information: It has been 9 years and the family of Suraya Deedat is still looking for answers. The bodies of the 37-year-old mother and all four of her small children were found in their burnt-out home in Johannesburg. They were lying in a row in the lounge of the family home in Ormonde. All of them were lying on their backs facing the ceiling indicating that they were not close to an exit or escape at the time of the fire. The husband and father, Naeem Deedat escaped the house unharmed through a bathroom window. His clothes were not burnt and the bathroom from which he escaped was locked off from the rest of the house. A fridge was also found blocking the lounge door where the family was found. Naeem stated in an affidavit (that he changed 3 times) that the fire was started by a pillow that fell onto an electric heater. Naeem maintains to date that he could not save his family as the pillow ignited a fire that rapidly turned into a massive inferno. In 2017, Suraya’s family approached private investigator Paul O’Sullivan who opened the first inquest. But O’Sullivan was unable to decipher what happened on the night of the family’s deaths. The court ruled out murder and O’Sullivan dropped the case. His investigations however led him to Jacob Polela, a witness who later became central to the second inquest that was opened by private prosecutor, Gerrie Nel three years later. In February 2020 the second inquest started in the Johannesburg Magistrates court. Nel called various witnesses to the stand, including Jacob Polela. Polela alleges that he saw Naeem outside the house on the night of the fire. He testified that Naeem was looking into the house which was heavily locked from the outside. The inquest was halted before the lockdown as the court waited on the pathologist who performed the autopsies, to testify. The pathologist resides in Canada and will be testifying via Zoom in November.
